subject: DPA and KMS - HealthIQ transfer controls & TIA kickoff
messages:
From: Sam Peters <sam.peters@healthiq.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA: healthiq questions on KMS, SCCs and TIA

Irene —

Thanks for sending the draft DPA. A few things jumped out on our side that we need clarified before we can move procurement:

- Key management model: we typically require customer-managed keys for production PHI. Can you confirm whether Redwood supports customer-managed KMS (Azure Key Vault / AWS KMS) for envelope-wrapping model, and if so what the operational handoff looks like?
- Key rotation / escrow: we need a short note on your rotation cadence, and whether you support key escrow/backup for disaster recovery.
- SCCs route: does Redwood rely on Standard Contractual Clauses + TIA or do you leverage any UK Addendum? We need to know the exact transfer mechanism to show our legal team.
- Subprocessor updates: is there a 30-day notice window for new subprocessors? The draft DPA we received was silent on notification timing.

I attached our internal redline for reference (HealthIQ_DPA_redline_v2.docx) and a high-level dataflow we typically use. Can we get a short timeline — ideally a list of proposed changes from Redwood legal and an ETA for a TIA and any SOC2 evidence we can reasonably share? Procurement will need that to finalize the PO.

Procurement contact: purchasing@healthiq.com

Best,
Sam Peters
Senior Security Program Manager
HealthIQ

Attachment stubs: HealthIQ_DPA_redline_v2.docx (docx), healthiq-dataflow-v1.pdf (pdf)

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Sam Peters <sam.peters@healthiq.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA: healthiq questions on KMS, SCCs and TIA

Sam —

Thanks for the clear list. Looping in Ben (legal) and Marissa (privacy/ops) so we can answer in one place. High-level plan from Redwood:

1) KMS: we support both Redwood-managed and customer-managed key options. For customer-managed keys we support an envelope-wrapping model with AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault. Operational handoff: we will provide a short onboarding runbook and require a PKCS#12 (wrapped) exchange or cross-account IAM role depending on provider.

2) Rotation & escrow: Redwood rotates wrapping keys annually by default; we can adopt a custom rotation cadence in the Order Form. For escrow/DR we recommend storing a wrapped back-up key in a customer-controlled vault; Redwood can accept a temporary access grant in emergencies under strictly defined procedures.

3) SCCs/TIA: Redwood uses EU SCCs (2021 module 2 + SEV addenda where applicable) and produces a Transfer Impact Assessment summary for each customer in the EU by request. If HealthIQ needs the UK Addendum we can include it — please confirm.

4) Subprocessors: Redwood notifies customers of new subprocessors 30 days in advance for material subprocessors; for low-risk infra patches we do an internal notification stream. We can lock notification timing into the DPA per your procurement requirement.

Action items: Ben will propose DPA language for KMS and notification timing; Marissa will start a TIA draft and gather the SOC2 artifacts we can share; I can set up a 30-min sync with your procurement and security teams to align timelines.

How does Thursday 16 Sep at 11:00 AM CET / 02:00 AM PDT look for a quick call? Let me know a preferred time and I’ll calendar.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Senior Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference

Sam —

Appreciate the redline and dataflow. Quick legal note on the items you called out (Irene and Marissa, feel free to refine):

- Processor roles: we will accept the Order Form tying specific services to experimental vs production environments. We'll add a definition in the DPA that maps "Production" to your agreed Order Form SKUs.
- KMS/customer-managed: proposed clause: "Customer may elect to provide their own key material for envelope-wrapping; Redwood will only have access to wrapped keys and will not persist unwrapped key material." We will include operational steps and an emergency access carve-out requiring a court order + customer consent.
- Notification timelines: propose 30 days for new subprocessors; 48 hours for security incidents materially affecting data under the DPA.
- SCCs/TIA: we can include a short TIA appendix summarizing routing, logical separation, and any mitigations. For now we'll reference EU SCCs 2021 and offer to append the UK Addendum on request.

Please review the attached murky redline (HealthIQ_DPA_redline_v3.docx) — the redline includes placeholders where we need your preference (customer KMS vs Redwood KMS, logging export caps, retention carve-outs). If you confirm customer-managed KMS we can finalize the language and produce a TIA within 5 business days.

Procurement: if you can confirm the PO timeline and whether we should route through a marketplace listing (GCP/AWS) or direct invoicing that helps our billing team.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference
